The operators represent core probabilistic and decision-theoretic mechanisms within the system. The Poisson model encodes event likelihoods, enabling prediction of game outcomes through discrete probability mass functions. The Kelly optimizer maps these probabilities into optimal betting strategies, balancing risk and reward. Contextual scoring aggregates heterogeneous inputs—form, rest, line movement, data quality—into a unified signal. These primitives form a closed-loop system where probabilistic forecasts inform stake decisions, which in turn influence the feedback loop of model calibration and refinement. Dualities emerge in how uncertainty is quantified across both predictive and strategic dimensions. Failure modes include overfitting in Poisson modeling, misalignment in weight vectors, and incorrect application of Kelly when edge assumptions fail.
